Counting is easy if the numbers do not exceed ten.
INTRODUCTIONM
When numbers exceed 10, keeping track is harder.
The Decimal Number System helped to solve the problem of numbers larger than ten.
You use the Decimal Number System everyday.................
Computers and digital circuits do not use the Decimal Number System.
In this lesson you will learn how numbers are converted from one base to another.
Let's begin the lesson on NUMBER SYSTEMS..................................
LESSON MENU
There are 4 number systems used in digital electronics. They are:
DISCUSSION
The Decimal System is not new. You use the Decimal System almost everyday.
The Decimal System or base 10 uses ten digits. They are:...
Counting in the base 10 system begins at 0 and continues to 9. All 10 digits are written in the 1's column.
When the count of nine is exceeded, a zero is placed in the 1's column and a one is placed in the 10's column.
Each column added to the decimal chart is 10 times the value of the preceding column.
What is the decimal number if the count is increased by 1?
The Binary System is very common in digital electronics....
The Binary System or base 2 uses only two digits. They are:
Counting in the base 2 system begins at 0 and continues to 1. The 2 digits are written in the 1's column.
When the count of one is exceeded, a zero is placed in the 1's column and a one is placed in the 2's column.
Each column added to the binary chart is 2 times the value of the preceding column.
What is the binary number if the count is increased by 1?
When the count of 1 is exceeded, place a zero in that column and add one to the next higher column.
TRY AGAIN!
The Octal System is also common in digital electronics.....
The Octal System or base 8 uses eight digits. They are:....
Counting in the base 8 system begins at 0 and continues to 7. All 8 digits are written in the 1's column.
When the count of seven is exceeded, a zero is placed in the 1's column and a one is placed in the 8's column.
Each column added to the octal chart is 8 times the value of the preceding column.
What is the octal number if the count is increased by 1?
Remember, the highest number in octal is 7. When the count of 7 is exceeded, place a zero in that column and add one to the next higher column.
TRY AGAIN!
The Hexadecimal System is also common in digital electronics.
The Hexadecimal System or base 16 uses sixteen digits. They are:
Note that the numbers ten through fifteen are represented by the letters A through F.
Counting in the base 16 system begins at 0 and continues to fifteen (F). All 16 digits are written in the 1's column.
When the count of fifteen (F) is exceeded, a zero is placed in the 1's column and a one is placed in the 16's column.
Each column added to the hexadecimal chart is 16 times the value of the preceding column.
What is the hexadecimal number if the count is increased by 1?
When the count of fifteen (F) is exceeded, place a 0 in that column and add 1 to the next higher column. Remember, letters (A-F) represent the numbers 10 through 15.
TRY AGAIN!
Learn to identify the 4 number systems used in digital electronics. In the next objective you will learn to use the Binary Number System.

NUMBER CONVERSIONSE
The first step in converting one base system to another is to learn to count in both number systems.
DISCUSSION
In base ten when the count reaches nine, a place holder or zero is put in the 1's column. The count starts at 1 again in the 10's column.
In base two when the count reaches one, a place holder or zero is put in the 1's column. The count starts at 1 again in the 2's column.
Each time a column exceeds the base number the next column must be used.
Construct a number line by multiplying each column value by base 2 to find the next higher column value.
Let's convert the decimal number 21 to binary.
Find the largest column value that will not exceed the number 21 and place a 1 in that column. Subtract 16 from 21.
Find the largest column value that will not exceed the number 5 and place a 1 in that column. Subtract 4 from 5.
Note, if a column is skipped, put a place holder (0) in the column.
Find the largest column value that will not exceed the number 1 and place a 1 in that column.
